fullPassage: What do you think good design is? Some might assert good design makes products easy to use, while others might say good design is stylish or innovative. There are even some who believe that good design should be as environmentally friendly as possible. All of these are important elements of design. However, there is a new idea called “universal design.” This idea suggests that design should go beyond mere pretty looks and functions. Universal design takes into account the diverse needs of different people and includes features that make it possible for them to access and use products without any barriers. Now let’s take a look at how universal design is tackling the problem of limited access and reshaping the design of products and services. Universal design suggests that design be as flexible as possible so that it can accommodate diverse needs and a wide range of individual preferences. This could involve providing a variety of options for customization or adding adjustable features to a product. Take a look at the scissors, the computer mouse, and the desk pictured below. Do you notice how they differ from the more common types of scissors, mice, and desks? They are all designed for left-handed people. Without them, about 10% of the world’s population, who are left-handed, would find these simple products difficult to use. The height-adjustable desk is also a good example of a universal design that accommodates a wide range of individual preferences and abilities. If the desk is too high or too low, the users can adjust it to the heights they want. If desired, the user can work while standing. A wheelchair user is also able to use the desk at a comfortable height. Universal design also ensures that an environment or product is accessible to everyone. Anyone should be able to use a design regardless of who they are and what they’re capable of, and no one should be excluded. Curb cuts are a good example. Without curb cuts, people in wheelchairs would have a hard time navigating the city. Curb cuts eliminate barriers not only for wheelchair users but also for people moving heavy loads or riding bikes. Like curb cuts, automatic doors in public buildings also allow all people to enter without any major problems. Another characteristic of universal design is requiring low physical effort. Universal design seeks to create products that can be used efficiently and comfortably without causing unnecessary fatigue. Undoubtedly, many people have had trouble trying to open a lid of a jar that was stuck. Opening a lid can be a great challenge to people with a weak grip, the elderly, or people with hand or finger impairments. Fortunately, various clever opening devices have been designed. A lever-type door handle, which requires no firm grip or twisting, is also an example that reflects this characteristic of universal design. A door with a lever-type door handle can be opened using an elbow or a closed hand, which benefits people carrying baskets as well as those with limited strength in their hands. Universal design is not limited to the design of physical products or facilities. Universal design pushes for designs in which critical information is conveyed well, regardless of the surrounding environment or the user’s sensory abilities. Information should be conveyed not just through written language but also through universal symbols and audio cues. For instance, when it comes to foreign travelers, finding a restroom is much easier when they can simply look for the universally recognized restroom symbol rather than trying to interpret the local language. For those with visual or audio impairments, bus and subway arrival times are not only presented on electronic boards but also called out through voice announcements. In elevators, braille, which indicates the floor number, allows individuals with visual impairments to select their desired floor. Additionally, audio announcements confirm the selected floor and tell passengers when the elevator has reached their desired floor. As such, providing information in these diverse forms ensures that everyone can access and understand important information, regardless of language barriers, sensory impairments, etc. Universal design is beneficial to everyone. With universal design, no one needs to put up with unnecessary discomfort. The supporters of universal design suggest that it should be part of every design. Take a look around you. Is there anything that needs improvement so that it can be accessible to more people? If so, why not create a design and bring joy to more people?

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: who believes → who believe (선행사 some은 복수)
det.analysis:
① makes: 'good design makes products easy to use'는 'make + 목적어 + 형용사(…을 ~하게 만들다)' 구문이고, 주어 good design이 단수라 makes가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② who believes → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'some who ___ that good design should be ...'에서 관계대명사 who의 선행사는 some(사람들, 복수)이에요. 복수 선행사를 받으므로 관계절 동사도 believe가 되어야 하고, 단수형 believes는 틀려요. ❌ ←정답

③ called: 'a new idea called "universal design"'은 idea를 꾸미는 과거분사(~라고 불리는)라 called가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ should go: 'design should go beyond mere pretty looks'는 조동사 should 뒤 동사원형이라 should go가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 관계절 동사는 선행사의 수에 일치 → some who believe(복수).

Anyone should be able to use a design regardless of who they are and what they’re capable of, and no one ②<u>should be excluded</u>.  Curb cuts are a good example.  Without curb cuts, people in wheelchairs ③<u>would had</u> a hard time navigating the city.  Curb cuts eliminate barriers not only for wheelchair users but also for people ④<u>moving</u> heavy loads or riding bikes.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: would had → would have (조동사 뒤 동사원형)
det.analysis:
① is accessible: 'an environment or product is accessible to everyone'에서 주어가 단수로 취급되어 is가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② should be excluded: 'no one should be excluded'는 '배제되어서는 안 된다'라는 조동사 + 수동태(be + 과거분사)라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ would had → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'people in wheelchairs ___ a hard time navigating the city'는 '~라면 어려움을 겪을 것이다'라는 가정의 의미로 조동사 would를 써요. 조동사 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 would have가 되어야 하고, would had는 틀려요. ❌ ←정답

④ moving: 'people moving heavy loads or riding bikes'는 people을 꾸미는 현재분사로, 뒤의 riding과 병렬이라 moving이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 조동사(would) 뒤에는 동사원형 → would have a hard time.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: can be using → can be used (조동사 수동태)
det.analysis:
① seeks to create: 'Universal design seeks to create products'에서 seek은 to부정사를 목적어로 취하므로 seeks to create가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② can be using → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'products that ___ efficiently and comfortably'에서 제품은 '사용되는' 대상이므로 조동사 + 수동태(can be + 과거분사)가 되어야 해요. 따라서 can be used가 맞고, can be using은 틀려요. ❌ ←정답

③ have had: 'many people have had trouble trying to open a lid'는 현재완료(have + 과거분사 had)라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ have been designed: 'various clever opening devices have been designed'는 현재완료 수동태(have been + 과거분사)라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 조동사 + 수동태: can be used(사용될 수 있다). 주어가 '사용되는' 대상이에요.

det.korean: rigid → flexible: 디자인은 가능한 한 '유연'해야 한다
det.analysis:
① rigid → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'Universal design suggests that design be as ___ as possible so that it can accommodate diverse needs'에서 다양한 요구를 수용하려면 디자인이 '유연한(flexible)' 것이 적절해요. '경직된(rigid)'은 다양한 요구 수용과 정반대예요. ❌ ←정답

② customization: 'providing a variety of options for customization'은 '맞춤 설정'을 위한 선택지를 제공한다는 뜻이라 적절해요. ✅ 올바름

③ adjustable: 'adding adjustable features to a product'는 '조절 가능한' 기능을 더한다는 뜻이라 적절해요. ✅ 올바름

④ left-handed: 'They are all designed for left-handed people'은 '왼손잡이'를 위해 설계되었다는 뜻이라 적절해요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 다양한 요구를 수용하려면 → flexible(유연한) ↔ rigid(경직된).

questions.passage: Universal design is not limited to the design of physical products or facilities. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: harder → easier: 기호를 쓰면 화장실을 '더 쉽게' 찾는다
det.analysis:
① critical: 'designs in which critical information is conveyed well'은 '중요한' 정보가 잘 전달되는 디자인이라는 뜻이라 적절해요. ✅ 올바름

② harder → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'finding a restroom is much ___ when they can simply look for the ... restroom symbol'에서 보편적 기호를 쓰면 외국인 여행자가 화장실을 '더 쉽게(easier)' 찾을 수 있다는 뜻이에요. '더 어렵게(harder)'는 정반대예요. ❌ ←정답

③ recognized: 'the universally recognized restroom symbol'은 '보편적으로 인식되는' 기호라는 뜻이라 적절해요. ✅ 올바름

④ presented: 'bus and subway arrival times are not only presented on electronic boards'는 전광판에 '표시된다'는 뜻이라 적절해요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 보편적 기호를 쓰면 → easier(더 쉬운) ↔ harder(더 어려운).

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 adjust it to the heights they want(원하는 높이로 조절하다)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① replace it with a brand-new one(새 것으로 교체하다): 교체가 아니라 조절이 핵심이에요.

❌ ② return it to the store(상점에 반품하다): 반품과 무관해요.

✅ ③ adjust it to the heights they want(원하는 높이로 조절하다): 앞에서 '높이 조절 책상(height-adjustable desk)'을 소개했고, 'If the desk is too high or too low(너무 높거나 낮으면)'가 이어지므로, 사용자는 '원하는 높이로 조절할' 수 있어요. ← 정답

❌ ④ paint it a different color(다른 색으로 칠하다): 색칠과 무관해요.
det.tip: height-adjustable desk(높이 조절 책상) → 원하는 높이로 조절하다(adjust to the heights they want).

det.korean: 빈칸에 without causing unnecessary fatigue(불필요한 피로를 유발하지 않고)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① by requiring strong physical force(강한 물리적 힘을 요구함으로써): '낮은 신체적 노력'이라는 특징과 정반대예요.

❌ ② only with help from experts(전문가의 도움을 받아야만): 본문에 없는 내용이에요.

❌ ③ after a long installation process(긴 설치 과정을 거쳐야): 설치 과정과 무관해요.

✅ ④ without causing unnecessary fatigue(불필요한 피로를 유발하지 않고): 바로 앞에서 유니버설 디자인의 특징이 '낮은 신체적 노력(low physical effort)'이라 했으므로, 제품은 '불필요한 피로 없이' 효율적·편안하게 사용될 수 있어야 해요. ← 정답
det.tip: low physical effort(낮은 신체적 노력) → 피로 없이(without causing unnecessary fatigue).

④ 점자·음성 안내는 사례일 뿐 기술 발전사를 다루지 않아요.
det.tip: 마지막 문단 'no one needs to put up with unnecessary discomfort ... part of every design'이 주제를 압축해요.

ch: 모두가 장벽 없이 접근하고 사용할 수 있게 하는 유니버설 디자인의 특징과 가치
왼손잡이 전용 제품의 상업적 성공 사례에 대한 분석
공공건물 자동문의 전력 소비를 줄이는 구체적 방법
점자와 음성 안내 기술이 발전해 온 역사적 과정

questions.passage: However, there is a new idea called “universal design. ” This idea suggests that design should go beyond mere pretty looks and functions.  Universal design takes into account the diverse needs of different people and includes features that make it possible for them to access and use products without any barriers.  Now let’s take a look at how universal design is tackling the problem of limited access and reshaping the design of products and services.  Universal design suggests that design be as flexible as possible so that it can accommodate diverse needs and a wide range of individual preferences.
questions.stem: 위 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 글 전체를 아우르는 제목.
det.analysis:
❌ ① A Simple Guide to Buying the Right Desk(알맞은 책상을 사는 간단 안내서): 책상은 한 사례일 뿐이에요.

❌ ② The Hidden Cost of Modern Architecture(현대 건축의 숨은 비용): 비용을 다루는 글이 아니에요.

✅ ③ Universal Design: Products Everyone Can Use(유니버설 디자인: 모두가 쓸 수 있는 제품): 글은 누구나 장벽 없이 쓸 수 있게 하는 유니버설 디자인을 다루므로 제목으로 가장 적절해요. ← 정답

❌ ④ How Automatic Doors Changed City Life(자동문이 도시 생활을 바꾼 방식): 자동문은 한 사례일 뿐이에요.
det.tip: 핵심은 'Universal Design(유니버설 디자인)'과 'Everyone Can Use(모두가 쓸 수 있는)'예요.

ch: A Simple Guide to Buying the Right Desk
The Hidden Cost of Modern Architecture
Universal Design: Products Everyone Can Use
How Automatic Doors Changed City Life

questions.passage: Universal design also ensures that an environment or product is accessible to everyone.  Anyone should be able to use a design regardless of who they are and what they’re capable of, and no one should be excluded.  Curb cuts are a good example.  Without curb cuts, people in wheelchairs would have a hard time navigating the city.  Curb cuts <u>eliminate barriers</u> not only for wheelchair users but also for people moving heavy loads or riding bikes.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>eliminate barriers</u>가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 밑줄 구절이 비유하는 '장벽 제거'.
det.analysis:
'eliminate barriers'의 barriers는 물리적 담장만이 아니라 사람들의 이동·접근을 '가로막는 장애물'을 뜻하는 비유예요.

❌ ① 연석을 전부 철거: 커브 컷은 연석을 '잘라 경사로를 만드는' 것이지 전부 없애는 것이 아니에요.

❌ ② 휠체어를 저렴하게 생산: 제품 생산과 무관해요.

❌ ③ 출입을 엄격히 통제: 접근을 '막는' 것이라 정반대예요.

✅ ④ 다양한 사람들의 이동과 접근을 가로막는 장애물을 없애는 것: 커브 컷이 휠체어 이용자뿐 아니라 짐을 옮기는 사람·자전거 이용자의 '장애물'을 없앤다는 맥락과 맞아요. ← 정답
det.tip: barriers = 물리적·현실적 '접근 장애물'. eliminate barriers = 그 장애물을 없애다.

ch: 도로의 연석을 전부 철거해 길을 완전히 평평하게 만드는 것
휠체어를 훨씬 더 저렴하게 대량으로 생산하는 것
공공건물의 출입을 더 엄격하게 통제하는 것
다양한 사람들의 이동과 접근을 가로막는 장애물을 없애는 것

questions.passage: Universal design suggests that design be as flexible as possible so that it can accommodate diverse needs and a wide range of individual preferences.  This could involve providing a variety of options for customization or adding adjustable features to a product.  Take a look at the scissors, the computer mouse, and the desk pictured below.  Do you notice how they differ from the more common types of scissors, mice, and desks?  They are all designed for left-handed people.  <u>Without them</u>, about 10% of the world’s population, who are left-handed, would find these simple products difficult to use.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 부분에서 <u>Without them</u>의 them이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: them이 가리키는 대상.
det.analysis:
앞에서 소개한 가위·마우스·책상은 'They are all designed for left-handed people(모두 왼손잡이를 위해 설계된 것)'이라고 했어요.

✅ ① 왼손잡이를 위해 설계된 제품들: 'Without them, ... left-handed people would find these simple products difficult to use'의 them은 그 왼손잡이용 제품들을 가리켜요. ← 정답

❌ ② 왼손잡이 인구: 사람이 아니라 '제품'을 가리켜요.

❌ ③ 더 흔한 일반 제품: 오히려 왼손잡이가 쓰기 어려워하는 제품이에요.

❌ ④ 높이 조절 책상의 기능: 뒤에 나오는 다른 사례예요.
det.tip: them은 바로 앞의 '왼손잡이용으로 설계된 제품들'을 받는 대명사예요.

ch: 높이 조절 책상이 제공하는 다양한 기능

questions.passage: For instance, when it comes to foreign travelers, finding a restroom is much easier when they can simply look for the universally recognized restroom symbol rather than trying to interpret the local language.  For those with visual or audio impairments, bus and subway arrival times are not only presented on electronic boards but also called out through voice announcements.  In elevators, braille, which indicates the floor number, allows individuals with visual impairments to __________.  Additionally, audio announcements confirm the selected floor and tell passengers when the elevator has reached their desired floor.  As such, providing information in these diverse forms ensures that everyone can access and understand important information, regardless of language barriers, sensory impairments, etc. Universal design is beneficial to everyone.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 select their desired floor(원하는 층을 선택하다)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① clean the elevator car quickly(엘리베이터를 빠르게 청소하다): 청소와 무관해요.

✅ ② select their desired floor(원하는 층을 선택하다): 'braille, which indicates the floor number, allows individuals with visual impairments to __________'에서 점자가 '층 번호를 알려 주므로', 시각 장애인은 '원하는 층을 선택할' 수 있어요. ← 정답

❌ ③ repair the control panel easily(제어판을 쉽게 수리하다): 수리와 무관해요.

❌ ④ count the waiting crowd outside(밖에서 기다리는 사람 수를 세다): 문맥과 무관해요.
det.tip: braille indicates the floor number(점자가 층 번호를 알려 줌) → 원하는 층을 선택하다.

questions.passage: What do you think good design is?  Some might assert good design makes products easy to use, while others might say good design is stylish or innovative.  There are even some who believe that good design should be as environmentally friendly as possible.  __________.  However, there is a new idea called “universal design.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 바탕으로, 다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오. (영어로)

'이 모든 것이 디자인의 중요한 요소이다.'

[조건]
(1) All, are, design, elements, important, of, of, these 를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 8단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 이 모든 것이 디자인의 중요한 요소이다.
det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- All of these(주어): 이 모든 것
- are(동사): ~이다 (주어가 복수 개념이라 are)
- important elements of design(보어): 디자인의 중요한 요소
→ 'All of + 복수 명사'는 복수 취급하므로 be동사는 are를 써요.
det.tip: All of these + 복수동사 are. '이 모든 것이 ~이다'.

questions.wa: All of these are important elements of design
accept: All of these are important elements of design

questions.passage: Universal design also ensures that an environment or product is accessible to everyone. Anyone should be able to use a design regardless of who they are and what they are capable of, and no one should be __________ (exclude).
questions.stem: 다음 글의 흐름에 맞도록 괄호 안에 주어진 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.korean: '누구도 배제되어서는 안 된다'가 되도록 exclude를 변형.
det.analysis: 구문 분석: 'no one should be ___'에서 주어 no one은 '배제되는' 대상이므로 수동태(should be + 과거분사)를 써야 해요. exclude의 과거분사는 excluded이므로 should be excluded(배제되어서는 안 된다)가 돼요.
det.tip: 조동사 + 수동태(be + 과거분사): should be excluded. exclude → excluded.

questions.passage: Curb cuts are a good example.  Without curb cuts, people in wheelchairs would have a hard time navigating the city.  Curb cuts eliminate barriers not only for wheelchair users but also for people moving heavy loads or riding bikes.  Like curb cuts, __________ without any major problems.  Another characteristic of universal design is requiring low physical effort.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 바탕으로, 다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오. (영어로)

'공공건물의 자동문은 또한 모든 사람이 들어갈 수 있게 한다.'

[조건]
(1) all, allow, also, automatic, buildings, doors, enter, in, people, public, to 를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 11단어로 쓸 것 (allow + 목적어 + to부정사 구문을 사용할 것)

det.korean: 공공건물의 자동문은 또한 모든 사람이 들어갈 수 있게 한다.
det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- automatic doors in public buildings(주어 + 전치사구): 공공건물의 자동문은
- also allow(동사): 또한 ~할 수 있게 한다
- all people(목적어): 모든 사람이
- to enter(목적격보어, to부정사): 들어가도록
→ 'allow + 목적어 + to부정사(~가 …하도록 허용하다)' 구문이에요.
det.tip: allow + O + to V: allow all people to enter(모든 사람이 들어갈 수 있게 하다).

questions.wa: automatic doors in public buildings also allow all people to enter
accept: automatic doors in public buildings also allow all people to enter

questions.passage: Another characteristic of universal design is requiring low physical effort.  Universal design seeks to create products that can be used efficiently and comfortably without causing unnecessary fatigue.  Undoubtedly, many people have had trouble trying to open a lid of a jar that was stuck.  __________ with a weak grip, the elderly, or people with hand or finger impairments.  Fortunately, various clever opening devices have been designed.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 올바른 순서로 배열하시오. (정확히 10단어, 영어로)

'뚜껑을 여는 것은 사람들에게 큰 어려움이 될 수 있다.'

[단어] a / a / be / can / challenge / great / lid / Opening / people / to

det.korean: 뚜껑을 여는 것은 사람들에게 큰 어려움이 될 수 있다.
det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- Opening a lid(동명사 주어): 뚜껑을 여는 것은
- can be(조동사 + be): ~이 될 수 있다
- a great challenge(보어): 큰 어려움
- to people(전치사구): 사람들에게
→ 동명사구가 주어 자리에 와서 '~하는 것은'이라는 의미를 만들고, can be 뒤에 보어가 이어져요.
det.tip: 동명사 주어(Opening a lid) + can be + 보어. '여는 것은 ~이 될 수 있다'.

questions.wa: Opening a lid can be a great challenge to people
accept: Opening a lid can be a great challenge to people

questions.passage: Without them, about 10% of the world’s population, who are left-handed, would find these simple products difficult to use.  The height-adjustable desk is also a good example of a universal design that accommodates a wide range of individual preferences and abilities.  If the desk is too high or too low, the users can adjust it to the heights they want.  If desired, the user can work while standing.  __________ at a comfortable height.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 바탕으로, 다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오. (영어로)

'휠체어 이용자도 그 책상을 사용할 수 있다.'

[조건]
(1) A, able, also, desk, is, the, to, use, user, wheelchair 를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 10단어로 쓸 것 (be able to 구문을 사용할 것)

det.korean: 휠체어 이용자도 그 책상을 사용할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- A wheelchair user(주어): 휠체어 이용자
- is also able to use(동사구): 또한 ~을 사용할 수 있다
- the desk(목적어): 그 책상을
→ 'be able to + 동사원형(~할 수 있다)' 구문이며, also는 '~도'라는 의미로 덧붙여요.
det.tip: be able to + 동사원형: is able to use(사용할 수 있다). also = ~도.

questions.wa: A wheelchair user is also able to use the desk
accept: A wheelchair user is also able to use the desk
